aws.title: [RESOLVED] Elevated API issues and Launch Failures
aws.update: Between 6:46 AM and 9:46 AM PST, we experienced elevated API error rates and launch failures primarily centered in a single Availability Zone (apne1-az1). We also experienced impact to other services such as ECS and Fargate Task Launch failures, ELB provisioning delays, Nat Gateway failures for Create and Disassociate workflows and Managed Flink application state transitions delays. Running EC2 instances and existing workflows were not affected. During this time, EC2 and EBS health data was missing or delayed for the affected Availability Zone resulting in CloudWatch alarms to transition to INSUFFICENT_DATA state and the DescribeInstanceStatus API to return Insufficient Data. We had identified the root cause and began our mitigation efforts by 7:47 AM, and by 9:46 AM we were seeing broad recovery for APIs and were able to see new EC2 launches succeed. aws.title: Region Availability
aws.update: We are providing an update on the disruption affecting the Middle East (UAE) (me-central-1) Region. After a thorough assessment, we have determined that we are unable to restore access to the resources and data hosted exclusively in the mec1-az2 Availability Zone. We continue to work on recovering regional resources, as well as zonal resources hosted in the other affected Availability Zones (mec1-az1 and mec1-az3). Since the disruption began in March, most customers have been able to re-establish their operations in other Regions by restoring backups or copying data that remained accessible. AWS Support remains available to help customers who need assistance moving their applications to alternate Regions. We remain committed to supporting our customers in the UAE. aws.title: Region Availability
aws.update: We are providing an update on the disruption affecting the Middle East (Bahrain) (me-south-1) Region. The damage to our infrastructure spanned multiple Availability Zones and exceeded what our regional and multi-AZ services are designed to withstand. After a thorough assessment, we have determined that we are unable to restore access to the resources and data hosted exclusively in this Region. When the first Availability Zone was damaged in March, we began recommending that customers migrate their workloads to other Regions, and most did so before the Region became unavailable following the disruption of a second Availability Zone in April. Since then, we have supported the remaining customers in re-establishing their operations in alternate Regions, using backups where available or implementing alternative solutions to mitigate the impact of inaccessible data.
